questions.question:
**Directions: Select the synonym of the given word.**

Nebulous
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Vague'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's see the meaning of the given words-
 
 
• **Nebulous**→ Vague or ill-defined (which is not clear)

 
 
• **Example**: The concept of time is often perceived as nebulous, as it is difficult to define and comprehend fully.
 
 
 
• **Faith**→ Complete trust or confidence
 
 
• Example: Despite facing numerous challenges, she held onto her faith, believing that everything would work out in the end.
 
 
 
• **Stable**→ Not likely to give way or overturn, firmly fixed.
 
 
• Example: The stock market showed stable growth over the past year, providing investors with a sense of security.
 
 
 
• **Dearly**→ Very much or at a great cost
 
 
• Example: He cherished his grandmother dearly, as she had always been there for him throughout his life.
 
 
 
• **Vague**→ Of uncertain or imprecise in thought or meaning.
 
 
• Example: The instructions given for the assignment were vague, leaving the students confused about what was expected of them.​
 
 
 
 
 
• So the correct answer is** 'Vague' as it is the exact synonym of the given word.**

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

__Since it falls__ on the floor, her dog, a black Labrador, gulped the biscuit down.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Since it fell'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The given phrase is to be replaced with **'Since it fell'**

 
• **In the given sentence **there are two clauses** the main clause** is 'Her dog, a black Labrador, gulped the biscuit down.' and** the subordinate clause** is 'Since it falls on the floor'
 
• As we can see that the main clause's verb is in the past tense the verb is 'gulped' so according to the rule of grammar the subordinate clause should be in the past tense.
 
• So we should replace 'falls' with 'fell'

**So the correct sentence is- *****Since it fell** on the floor, her dog, a black Labrador, gulped the biscuit down. *

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence.**

The police brought a search warrant when they raided his house.

options.text: A search warrant had been brought when the police raided his house.
The police had raided his house and brought a search warrant.
A search warrant was brought by the police when they raided his house.
A search warrant was brought when they raided his house by the police.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'A search warrant was brought by the police when they raided his house.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **According to the rule of grammar,** the subject of the sentence is 'the police' and the object of the sentence is 'a search warrant' hence the rule says that in the passive voice the subject of the sentence becomes the object and the object of the sentence becomes the subject.
 
• *The main verb of the sentence is 'Brought' which tells that it is in the past tense hence in the passive voice the tense will not be changed.*
 
• *Also, the sequence of the clauses should not be changed too. 'When they raided his house' should be at the end position.*

**So the correct sentence is-** *A search warrant was brought by the police when they raided his house.* i.e.* *option 3.* *

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Most of voters in Taiwan seem to have once again voted for the democratic party and President Tsai Ing-wen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Most of voters' i.e. error lies in this part of the sentence.**

***__Key Points__**

**In the given sentence, **the usage of **'Most of voters'** is incorrect instead use **'Most voters'**

__
 
• **According to grammar,** '**Most' is a determiner** which is used for the nouns to determine them as it is determiner hence it has no effect on the verb. 
 
• If we read further the verb of the sentence is 'seem' which is a plural verb. So the subject of the sentence should be a plural noun which is going to be 'Voters'

**So the correct sentence is-** ***Most voters** in Taiwan seem to have once again voted for the democratic party and President Tsai Ing-wen.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__***

 
• **'Most of' is also a quantifier** and the structure is Most of + definite article + noun. In this case, the verb should be according to the noun.*
 
• *Let's see an example-*
 
 
• *​***Most of the houses** in the capital don't **have** piped water. 
 
 
 
• **So the given sentence can also be corrected in the other way also-** *Most of the voters in Taiwan seem to have once again voted for the democratic party and President Tsai Ing-wen.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

We noticed that most of the shoppers in the mall looking for packets of ready to cook food.

options.text: packets of ready to cook food

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'in the mall looking for'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

** In the given sentence,** the usage of **'in the mall looking for**' is incorrect Instead, use **'in the mall were looking for'**

 
• **According to grammar,** **'Most of'** is a quantifier which is used to **'to refer to the majority of a group of things or people or the largest part of something.'**
 
• **In the given sentence,** **'that clause'** is used which has its own subject which is 'shoppers' hence we need a verb for this subject because it is not mentioned in the sentence. 
 
• *So we need a plural verb which should be in the past tense because the main clause of the sentence is in the past tense.*
 
• So use **'were looking'**

**So the correct sentence is- ***We noticed that most of the shoppers in the mall **were looking for** packets of ready to cook food.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. I sow a seed.

B. I saw the sapling.

C. I saw the sprout.

D. I saw the plant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'ACBD'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's first understand the meaning of the given words which are given in the sentences-
 
 
• **Seed**→ A seed is the small, hard part of a plant from which a new plant grows.
 
• **Sapling**→ A sapling is a young tree.
 
• **Sprout**→ When plants, vegetables, or seeds sprout, they produce new shoots or leaves.
 
• **Plant**→ A plant is a living thing that grows in the earth and has a stem, leaves, and roots.
 
 
 
• **Hence according to the meaning of the words→ **
 
 
• *We put seed, then sprout will grow or develop, then sapling will come out a small plant and then the plant.*
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-*** I sow a seed I saw the sprout I saw the sapling I saw the plant.*
